lines: Scout's home and Route 10 is back to its regular amount of chaos. Best kind there is.
Well, would you look at that. Get Scout along to Nora — she's on the patio at Stamford Coffee, up Main.
Sounds like you're closing in on Scout. My money's on the mill pond in Jefferson — every dog ends up there.
Bring him back to Nora when you have him. She's on the patio at Stamford Coffee, along Main here.
So Renata saw him Wednesday — he's working his way north, then. Try Dot, outside Middle Brook Cafe in Jefferson.
And Nora's waiting on the patio at Stamford Coffee, right here in the village, whenever you find him.
Start with Renata at Cellar Door Wines, down in Hobart. She's the one who saw Scout last.
See the flyers? Scout's been loose since Tuesday — grey muzzle, and one ear that stands straight up.
Half the county has spotted Scout by now, and not one of us has managed to get a hand on him.
Start with Renata at Cellar Door Wines, down in Hobart. He was in her shop yesterday, bold as you like.
Glad Scout's story ends the way it should. Come back to Cellar Door for a tasting once things settle.
There's Scout! I knew he'd turn up looking pleased with himself. Give Nora my love when you see her.
Told you — Scout had that bench to himself a good ten minutes. Next is Dot, outside Middle Brook Cafe in Jefferson.
Oh, Scout! Grey muzzle, one ear straight up — he came up onto the patio Wednesday and sat by the bench like a customer.
Then he trotted off up Route 10, heading north. Ask Dot, outside Middle Brook Cafe in Jefferson — nothing gets past her.
Welcome to Cellar Door — take your time. If it's news you're after, Earl holds court outside Stewart's in Stamford.
I'll bet Scout is home by now, causing a whole new kind of trouble, and Nora couldn't be happier about it.
You found Scout?! Get him to Nora — she's on the patio at Stamford Coffee, down in Stamford. Go on, quick.
The mill pond, past the Mill Pond Inn at the west end of Main Street. Scout loves that shade by the water.
Scout! He was right outside our window yesterday, ear straight up, gone up Main Street before anyone could set down a cup.
Try the mill pond, past the Mill Pond Inn, at the west end of Main Street. There's shade by the water there.
You're after Scout too? Renata at Cellar Door Wines, down in Hobart, saw him before I did. Start there.
Big week in Jefferson. Ask Earl — he's outside Stewart's up in Stamford, and he'll tell it better than I would.
Scout hasn't left my side since. Thank you again — and that offer of a coffee does not expire.
Scout! Oh — oh, thank you. I have sat on this patio all week asking everybody who walked past.
Sit down a minute, would you — anything you like from the counter is on me. I mean that, truly.

effects.toast: Episode complete — new story next week

lines: Still no Scout. He slipped out of the yard on Tuesday and I have asked everyone up and down Route 10 since.
Somebody has seen him, I know it. Scout has never once passed a village quietly in his life.
Have you seen a scruffy dog, grey muzzle, one ear straight up? That's Scout. He slipped the yard on Tuesday.
I have been asking up and down Route 10 all week. Try Earl, outside Stewart's — he hears every sighting first.
A scruffy dog is stretched out in the shade by the mill pond: grey muzzle, one ear straight up, thoroughly content.
Scout trots over like he had been expecting you all along, and falls in beside you as though it were his idea.
A hand-drawn flyer taped inside the window: LOST DOG — SCOUT. GREY MUZZLE, ONE EAR UP. ANSWERS WHEN IT SUITS HIM.
The same flyer on the corkboard by the register, with a line added underneath: "still out here having the time of his life."
Taped to the door: the same LOST DOG flyer, and a little pencil sketch someone has added of Scout in sunglasses, ear up.
Someone's chalked a small paw print in the corner of the tavern's board, for luck.
